Topics · Hard times

Why doesn't God stop people from doing harm?

Freedom explains much harm. It excuses no one, says nothing against the hurt, and leaves a hard question open.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عَيْنَيْنِ٨ وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ٩ وَهَدَيْنَـٰهُ ٱلنَّجْدَيْنِ١٠﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have We not made for him two eyes? And a tongue and two lips? And have shown him the two ways?[1925]

Translator's notes

[1925] Of good and evil.

Quran · Al-Balad 90:8-10

Translation

Behold, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil. I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants,

Original · Hebrew

רְאֵ֨ה נָתַ֤תִּי לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֶת־הַֽחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַטּ֑וֹב וְאֶת־הַמָּ֖וֶת וְאֶת־הָרָֽע׃ הַעִידֹ֨תִי בָכֶ֣ם הַיּוֹם֮ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ֒ הַחַיִּ֤ים וְהַמָּ֨וֶת֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לְפָנֶ֔יךָ הַבְּרָכָ֖ה וְהַקְּלָלָ֑ה וּבָֽחַרְתָּ֙ בַּֽחַיִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן תִּחְיֶ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה וְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 30:15, 19

World English Bible

Start with what you know from inside. You have weighed two courses and taken one. That is what gives kindness its worth. A person who cannot do otherwise is not kind, only set that way. Now the hard step: a world where love is really chosen is a world where it can be refused, and a refusal can land on someone innocent. Many philosophers hold that this answers the claim that God and evil cannot both exist. It answers that claim only. It does not make the harm acceptable.

A question for you

Would you give up your own freedom for a world with no cruelty?

If you sayYes, without hesitating.
ThenMany who have suffered would say the same, and it is no small wish. It is the strongest thing to say against this argument.
If you sayNo, though part of me wishes I could.
ThenThen you feel the weight of both sides, which is where this argument really stands.
If you sayI do not think that is a fair choice.
ThenThat is close to Mackie's objection: why were we not made free and always choosing well?

Part 2 of 3

﴿إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا ٱلْأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلْجِبَالِ فَأَبَيْنَ أَن يَحْمِلْنَهَا وَأَشْفَقْنَ مِنْهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومًا جَهُولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, We offered the Trust[1214] to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.[1215]

Translator's notes

[1214] The acceptance of obligations and obedience to Allāh. [1215] Coveting its reward while forgetting the penalty for failure to keep his commitment.

Quran · Al-Ahzab 33:72

﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَـَٔامَنَ مَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا ۚ أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ ٱلنَّاسَ حَتَّىٰ يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Then, [O Muḥammad], would you compel the people in order that they become believers?

Quran · Yunus 10:99

Translation

But I was willing to do nothing without your consent, that your goodness would not be as of necessity, but of free will.

Original · Ancient Greek

χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·

Philemon · 1:14

World English Bible

The Quran does not hide the risk. It speaks of a trust from which the heavens, the earth and the mountains drew back. The human being took it up, and the verse says how much wrong can follow. It also says God could have made everyone believe. So the book does not claim He is unable to stop a hand. Why He does not stop this hand, on this day, the text does not say. That is the honest edge.

A question for you

Which part of this is hardest for you?

If you sayThat He could stop it and does not.
ThenThat is the centre of the matter, and no complete answer is known. The objection stands here.
If you sayThat people do this to each other.
ThenThat is a different grief, and the next part turns to it.
If you sayThat freedom is called a trust at all.
ThenIt is a strange word for something so costly. Notice what it implies: whoever holds a trust will answer for it.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَـٰفِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ ۚ إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And never think that Allāh is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them [i.e., their account] for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror].

Quran · Ibrahim 14:42

Translation

Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil. Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him. But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow, because he doesn’t fear God.

Original · Hebrew

אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵין־נַעֲשָׂ֣ה פִתְגָ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מְהֵרָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֡ן מָלֵ֞א לֵ֧ב בְּֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֛ם בָּהֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֹטֶ֗א עֹשֶׂ֥ה רָ֛ע מְאַ֖ת וּמַאֲרִ֣יךְ ל֑וֹ כִּ֚י גַּם־יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה־טּוֹב֙ לְיִרְאֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽירְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃ וְטוֹב֙ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹֽא־יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִ֖ים כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יָרֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

Ecclesiastes · 8:11-13

World English Bible

There are two things this reasoning must never be used for. It must never excuse the one who did the harm: their freedom is why they are answerable. It must never touch the one who was hurt: what was done to them says nothing about them. The verse looks to the wrongdoer's future: God is not unaware, and what looks like escape is delay. That may not comfort everyone. It does say that what was done to you is seen, and that no one is calling it acceptable.

A question for you

What does this explain for you, and what does it leave out?

If you sayIt explains cruelty, not illness or disaster.
ThenThat is its boundary, and the next question lies beyond it.
If you sayIt explains nothing for me.
ThenThen the objection stays yours, and this page does not ask you to give it up.
If you sayIt helps me stop blaming myself.
ThenThat may be the best use it can have. Keep it.

The same in the other books
